system_description.narrative_title: Global bond rout: soaring yields and policy fallout
system_description.narrative_summary: Across the window the single dominant narrative is a global bond-market sell-off: benchmark sovereign yields have surged to multiyear highs, reverberating through mortgages, corporate borrowing costs, FX and safe-haven assets. As an open system this narrative links incoming macro datapoints (inflation, jobs), central-bank signaling, fiscal stress (notably in some European sovereigns), and cross-border capital flows; changes in any node feed back into expectations and prices elsewhere, creating reinforcing and balancing loops (e.g., higher yields -> tighter financial conditions -> growth/inflation impacts -> policy reaction).
system_description.scope: Sovereign and corporate bond markets and benchmark yields (US Treasuries, gilts, French debt, Asian sovereigns), central-bank policy expectations, interest-rate sensitive markets (mortgages, housing, corporate credit), investor flows (safe-haven shifts, quant/hedge activity), related asset reactions (equities, gold, FX), and short-term macro drivers (inflation reports, payrolls, fiscal announcements).
system_description.super_system: Global macro-financial system / global economy and financial stability
adjacent_subsystems: Monetary policy and central banks (Fed, ECB, BOJ, BoE)
Housing and consumer credit markets (mortgages, household balance sheets)
Equities and corporate credit (debt issuance, credit spreads)
Fiscal policy and sovereign debt management (government borrowing, budget credibility)

variables.name: Long-term nominal yields
variables.description: The prevailing interest rate on long-dated government and benchmark debt instruments measured as a continuous level across the yield curve's long end.

variables.name: Short-term policy rate expectations
variables.description: The market consensus or perceived path for short-term policy interest rates over the coming months.

variables.name: Headline inflation rate
variables.description: The observed rate of change in consumer prices across the economy over a defined recent period.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: The anticipated future inflation rate as reflected in surveys, market measures and investor pricing.

variables.name: Real economic growth rate
variables.description: The economy's inflation-adjusted output growth measured as a continuous rate of change.

variables.name: Financial conditions tightness
variables.description: An aggregate measure of how restrictive financing and market conditions are, incorporating rates, spreads, liquidity and valuations.

variables.name: Mortgage interest rates
variables.description: The prevailing interest rates charged on residential mortgage lending across maturities and products.

variables.name: Corporate credit spreads
variables.description: The premium borrowers in the corporate sector pay over benchmark government yields, measured continuously across credit quality and tenor.

variables.name: Sovereign fiscal stress
variables.description: The perceived and measured pressure on public finances, reflected in deficit/debt dynamics and market-implied solvency concerns.

variables.name: Cross-border capital flows
variables.description: Net private and public capital movements across jurisdictions over time, including portfolio and interbank flows.

variables.name: Bond market liquidity
variables.description: The ease and cost with which fixed-income instruments can be transacted without materially moving prices.

variables.name: Investor risk aversion
variables.description: The prevailing willingness of market participants to hold risky assets versus safe assets, reflected in demand and pricing behavior.

variables.name: Safe-haven asset demand
variables.description: The level of investor demand for assets perceived as low-risk stores of value during market stress.

variables.name: Leveraged fixed-income exposure
variables.description: The aggregate size of levered and margin-funded positions in fixed-income markets held by traders, funds and other investors.

variables.name: Equity market sensitivity to rates
variables.description: The degree to which equity valuations and price volatility respond to changes in interest rates and yield levels.

variables.name: Housing market activity
variables.description: Transaction volumes, listing behaviour and price momentum in the residential real estate market as a continuous activity level.

catalysts.title: FOMC December meeting (potential hike)
catalysts.description: The scheduled December FOMC meeting and attendant guidance that could crystallize a rate-hike decision and materially shift market expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Fed may skip October but pull rate hike trigger in December"; Fed officials signal hold or wait.

catalysts.title: Mid‑October inflation releases (US, major economies)
catalysts.description: Upcoming monthly inflation releases (CPI/PCE and comparable prints) that will reset investors' inflation and rate expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "This Datapoint Could Explain Soaring Bond Yields"; inflation data repeatedly cited versus yields.

catalysts.title: Large US Treasury auction schedule / supply
catalysts.description: Ongoing calendar of Treasury debt supply and large auctions that can pressure yields and liquidity if demand softens.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "U.S. Treasury Selloff Resumes"; coverage on supply and corporate mega‑deals squeezing markets (Paramount debt sale).

catalysts.title: French fiscal developments and auctions
catalysts.description: Near‑term fiscal announcements, debt auctions or policy disputes in France that amplify sovereign spread moves and market stress.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "France Is Ground Zero in the Global Bond Rout"; "French Yield Spreads Jump on Fiscal Worries."

catalysts.title: BOJ policy guidance / potential tightening
catalysts.description: Bank of Japan communications or policy shifts that could transmit to global yields and trigger cross‑border rebalancing.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "BOJ debated more rate hikes"; "Japan’s Bond Market Could Be the Next Catalyst for Global Yields."

catalysts.title: Volatility‑control funds rebalancing
catalysts.description: Volatility‑control strategies near record equity exposure could trigger rapid rebalancing into/out of bonds if market volatility spikes.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Volatility control funds near record equity exposure, raising selloff risk."

catalysts.title: UK autumn fiscal statement / gilt reaction
catalysts.description: UK fiscal announcements (autumn statement/budget updates) that could reignite gilt stress and bank funding concerns.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "UK banks tumble as gilt yields hit highest since 1998, budget jitters mount."
